LESSON: WRITING 8.5.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.5: Writing 8.5.1 Functional Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 8.5.1 Functional Writing, part of Strand 8 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How can we ensure that we write effective simple reports, memos and emails?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 8.5.1 Functional Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to Learn: The learner will reflect on their own work as they send one another emails with attachments.

● Self-efficacy-Personal skills: The learner will analyse their strengths and weaknesses as they write a simple report based

on the theme using the features identified.

Values:
● Unity: The learner cooperates with others to search online and offline for features of simple reports, memos and emails.

● Love: The learner respects others as they display the memo and conduct a gallery work.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship education: The learner portrays integrity and principles of leadership as they team up with others to search online

and offline for features of simple reports, memos and emails.

Suggested Learning Resources

● Print texts

● Digital devices with assistive technology

● Audio visual clips

Suggested Skills:

● Identify the elements of simple reports, memos and emails in written contexts.

● Write simple reports, memos and emails.
